definitions.explanation: Having insufficient light; not completely dark but lacking adequate brightness. Often describes twilight or shadowy environments.

examples.japanese: {夕方|ゆうがた}になって{辺|あた}りが{薄暗|うすぐら}くなった。
examples.english: It became dusky as evening approached.

examples.japanese: {薄暗|うすぐら}い{路地裏|ろじうら}を{一人|ひとり}で{歩|ある}くのは{怖|こわ}い。
examples.english: It's scary to walk alone through dimly lit back alleys.

notes:
FORMATION: Compound of {薄|うす}い (thin, faint) + {暗|くら}い (dark). The く becomes ぐ through rendaku (sequential voicing).

CONJUGATION: Regular i-adjective: {薄暗|うすぐら}くない, {薄暗|うすぐら}かった, {薄暗|うすぐら}くて, etc.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {薄暗|うすぐら}い{部屋|へや}/{廊下|ろうか}/{路地|ろじ} (dim room/hallway/alley)
- {薄暗|うすぐら}い{中|なか}で (in the dim light)
- {辺|あた}りが{薄暗|うすぐら}くなる (the area becomes dim)

RELATED WORDS:
- {暗|くら}い (dark - stronger darkness)
- {仄暗|ほのぐら}い (faintly dark - literary)
- ほの{暗|ぐら}い (dimly lit - alternative form)

forms.label: Conditional たら
forms.negative: {薄暗|うすぐら}くなかったら
